title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = -1 / x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = -1 / x, identify its symmetry, and specify the intervals over which the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.
finalAnswer: \text{Symmetric about the origin; Increasing on } (-\infty, 0) \text{ and } (0, \infty); \text{ Decreasing nowhere}

steps.title: Establish the Domain and Origin Symmetry
steps.explanation: The function is defined for all x != 0. Since f(-x) = -f(x), the function is odd and its hyperbolic graph in Quadrants II and IV is symmetric about the origin.
steps.why: Replacing (x, y) with (-x, -y) leaves the equation y = -1/x invariant.

steps.title: Test Monotonicity on (0, inf)
steps.explanation: On (0, inf), taking reciprocals reverses the inequality and multiplying by -1 reverses it a second time, restoring -1/x_1 < -1/x_2. Thus f is strictly increasing on (0, inf).
steps.why: Two successive inequality reversals preserve the original inequality direction.

steps.title: Test Monotonicity on (-inf, 0)
steps.explanation: Similarly, on (-inf, 0), as x increases from -infinity toward 0^-, -1/x increases from 0^+ toward +infinity. Therefore, f is increasing on (-inf, 0) and on (0, inf), and decreasing nowhere.
steps.why: Note that f is increasing on each interval (-inf, 0) and (0, inf) separately, though not across x = 0.
